summary: This study investigates the atomic layer deposition (ALD) of ZnO films using Zn(C2H5)2 and O3 as precursors and oxidant, respectively, at temperatures ranging from 230 to 300 8C. The self-limiting ALD mechanism was confirmed, and the growth rate decreased with increasing temperature. The films showed a c-axis preferential orientation and had different electrical properties compared to those using H2O as oxidant.
evidence: This study investigated the atomic layer deposition (ALD) behavior of zinc oxide (ZnO) films on SiO2/Si substrates using Zn(C2H5)2 and O3 as the precursor and oxidant, respectively, at substrate temperatures ranging from 230 to 300 8C, and the electrical properties of the thin films. The self-limiting ALD mechanism of ZnO thin film growth was confirmed in the whole temperature region, and the growth rate decreased from 0.19 nm/cycle at 230 8C to 0.16 nm/cycle at 300 8C. ZnO films with a c-axis preferential orientation were obtained at these relatively low temperatures.
